concepts.label: Capella Query tab (Web Console UI)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already established registry concept; this guide documents the Query tab's 'Index Advice' area/Build Suggested button as one of three equivalent ways to get index advice, matching how query-workbench.json already treats Index Advice as a facet of capella:query-tab rather than a separate concept

concepts.label: Index Advisor session (stateful, session-ID-addressed collection of ADVISOR() recommendations across multiple queries over a time window)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a genuinely new task-level concept. The reference page (advisor.json) modeled ADVISOR() as one function with several sub-usages; this guide reveals that the 'session' sub-usage is not just another function call but a distinct addressable, stateful object: the function returns a session ID on start, which must then be threaded through separate stop/get/list/purge/abandon actions performed later, and the session accumulates state (queries run during its window) independent of any single statement invocation. This is the strongest candidate in this batch for a genuine workflow/tooling concept that the SQL++ statement-reference layer does not fully capture on its own.

concepts.label: Couchbase SQL++ Index Advisor (standalone hosted web tool at index-advisor.couchbase.com)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a distinct external product from the in-cluster ADVISE/ADVISOR/Query-tab mechanisms; only ever appears as a Related Links pointer, but it is a genuinely separate 'thing' (a different tool, hosted separately, not part of the query-service runtime) rather than a synonym for the built-in features

notable_absence.finding: No privilege table, role requirement, or edition gate anywhere on this page for any of the three advice mechanisms (Query tab, ADVISE, ADVISOR()) - Index Advisor access appears ungated relative to ordinary query execution privileges, unlike the DDL statements (CREATE/DROP/ALTER INDEX) covered elsewhere in this batch.

cross_component_finding: Answering this round's specific question directly: index-advisor.md does introduce one genuinely new concept beyond restated statement/function vocabulary - the ADVISOR() session as a stateful, session-ID-addressed object with its own start/collect/stop/get/list/purge lifecycle (n1ql:advisor-session). The reference page (advisor.json) only flagged this as a function 'sub-usage'; this guide's procedural depth (worked examples chaining a returned session ID across three separate later calls) is what actually surfaces it as a distinct entity rather than just another function-call shape. The Query-tab UI mechanism and the standalone hosted tool (index-advisor.couchbase.com), by contrast, are genuinely separate surfaces worth noting but map cleanly onto the existing capella:query-tab concept (Query tab) or a single new external-tool pointer (index-advisor.couchbase.com) rather than revealing further hidden structure.
